A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable, complete 28-page versions of the same GR2R paper. Their corresponding main sections, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original denoising and inpainting experiments, including quantitative comparisons, reconstructed images and the parameter-sensitivity study in Appendix D.1.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and reports revised Gamma-denoising results in Tables 4 and 8 and Figures 3 and 9.

M1.justification: Table 1 rewrites the Poisson and Binomial splitting formulas using y instead of z; the stated relationships y = γz and y = z/ℓ make these algebraically equivalent. The losses, inference procedure and inverse-problem adaptation remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same DIV2K, SAR despeckling and fastMRI data, with the same denoising noise families and inpainting scenarios. The revised Gamma illustrations retain the same SAR scenes.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across corresponding experiments. In particular, Tables 4 and 8 retain Neigh2Neigh and Supervised-MSE alongside the two GR2R variants; the other denoising and inpainting comparisons also retain their original methods.

E3.justification: The reported protocols remain unchanged. Section 4.3 still specifies 127 SAR images, four look counts, 400 epochs, batch size 20, α = 0.2 and J = 10. No preprocessing, metric or experimental-setting change is disclosed to explain the revised Gamma results.

E4.justification: The α sensitivity study and log-Rayleigh moment-matching and histogram analyses in Appendices D.1–D.2 are unchanged. The Gamma revisions replace ordinary benchmark outputs for existing examples rather than adding an ablation, robustness test or distinct supplementary analysis.

E5.justification: Appendix D.3 reports PSNR means and standard deviations in both versions. Gamma standard-deviation values change, but the reporting practice remains the same; no changed run counts, seed information or statistical procedures are reported.

E6.justification: The Gamma-denoising evidence is substantially revised throughout Tables 4 and 8 and Figures 3 and 9. At ℓ = 30, GR2R-MSE changes from 42.37 ± 0.99 dB and 0.986 SSIM to 31.58 ± 1.72 dB and 0.901 SSIM. Every method's Gamma table values change, while GR2R-MSE remains the best self-supervised method. These are unexplained result replacements; the other experiments' results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The propositions, theorem, assumptions, proofs and derivations in the main text and Appendices A–B are unchanged. Table 1's equivalent algebraic rewrites and Section 3.2's explanation of conditional-distribution notation introduce no new mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: extending R2R beyond Gaussian noise, connecting it to supervised losses and SURE, introducing the NLL formulation and adapting it to inverse problems.

C2.justification: Interpretations of loss choice, α and inverse-problem applicability remain unchanged. Section 4.3 also retains its Gamma interpretation and the old 32.75 dB statement despite the revised tables.

D1.justification: The DRUnet/DnCNN assignments, DeepInverse implementation disclosure, training and inference details, maximum-entropy sampling instructions and code-access link are unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 35 references and research positioning are retained, including the relationship to earlier Poisson R2R extensions, SURE/GSURE and equivariant imaging.

P1.justification: v2 adds a short explanation of p(y1|y, α) in Section 3.2 and makes limited notation, caption and wording edits. Section organization and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 3 and 9 contain updated Gamma imagery and minor placement changes. Figure 9 loses its column headings, making method identification less explicit. Table 1 and nearby text receive small spacing adjustments; the overall figure and table organization is retained.

improvement.justification: v1's 32.75 dB Gamma statement agrees with its tables, whereas v2 retains that statement while Tables 4 and 8 report 22.19 dB for the corresponding methods. Figure 9 also loses its column labels. These introduced inconsistencies and reduced figure interpretability outweigh the small notation clarifications; the PDFs do not explain the substantial Gamma result replacement.
